title: Sub-Iterate Runner Result Contract
description: JSON schema for the result returned by sub-iterate-runner subagent. Used by the campaign loop to verify subagent output.

reviews.description: Review-cascade record per ADR-029. Optional for backwards-compat with pre-ADR-029 result.json files; required for runners under the post-ADR-029 contract.

plan.description: External Plan Review (Step 3.5 of sub-iterate-runner contract). Maps to references/iteration-planning.md Step 4.

self_review.description: Self-Review (Step 3.6 of sub-iterate-runner contract, post-ADR-029 follow-up). Mandatory at every complexity. Maps to references/iteration-reviews.md 7-item Self-Review Checklist (item 7 'Affected Boundaries' from ADR-024).

code.description: Internal code-reviewer subagent (Step 3.7a). This contract applies to the sub-iterate-runner in CAMPAIGN MODE only, where the runner has no Agent tool and the cascade is delegated to the orchestrator. A standalone iterate never reaches this contract — it spawns the cascade itself from SKILL.md Step 8. The runner must never report 'completed' here on the strength of the external review; that is external_code.

status.description: delegated_to_orchestrator is the campaign-only delegation. delegated_to_skill is DEPRECATED and invalid for new runs — it encoded a standalone delegation that had no delegate; the value is retained so historical result.json artifacts stay readable.

external_code.description: External LLM code review cascade (Step 3.7b). Maps to references/iteration-reviews.md 'External Code-Review Cascade'.

confidence_calibration.description: Confidence Calibration (Step 3.8 of sub-iterate-runner contract, post-ADR-029 follow-up). Empirical-probe phase mirroring SKILL.md Step 7.5 + references/confidence-anti-patterns.md asymptote heuristic. Mandatory at medium+ OR when touches_io_boundary is set OR when the user/orchestrator explicitly invokes a calibration probe (e.g. 'are you confident?').

risk_recheck.description: Post-Build diff-driven risk re-check (Step 3.4). Stage 1 classifies from the sub-iterate spec TEXT before code exists, so the diff-driven detectors (cross_component, touches_ci_supplychain, and the file-pattern halves of touches_io_boundary / touches_build) cannot fire for a campaign unit; Step 3.4 is the runner's Stage-2 equivalent. Optional for backwards-compat with pre-Step-3.4 result.json files, for the same reason `reviews` and `finalization` are optional — a schema that must still validate historical artifacts cannot enforce that a new mechanism ran. Execution is enforced by the runner contract and campaign-mode 3f-bis, not here.

finalization.description: Finalization record (iterate-2026-07-20-runner-finalization-integrity). Records that F3 (decision-drop), F5c (iterate entry), and the F6-verify self-verifier ran. Optional for backwards-compat; when present, verifier.exit_code MUST be 0 for a status:complete result.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable escalation cause. `complexity_large` is the original Step 2 case. `ci_supplychain_requires_operator` is the Step 3.4 case: the diff touches the CI trust boundary (.github/workflows/**, dependency-updater config, composite actions, shipped CI templates), which check_ci_supplychain_ack gates at EVERY complexity. The runner hands back rather than writing its own acknowledgement — the ack names the recorded posture decision a change agrees with, and a machine authoring its own permission slip defeats the gate (operator decision 2026-08-01).

detected_complexity.description: Widened beyond the original `large`-only enum: a Step 3.4 CI escalation can occur at any complexity, and reporting the value the re-check computed is more useful than omitting the field. Historical large-only results stay valid.

ci_paths.description: The CI trust-boundary files that forced the handback. Required and non-empty for a ci_supplychain_requires_operator escalation — an escalation naming no path is not actionable.
